lines.text: Hi, I'm Sindy! Today: an unmanaged cluster, where you set up Slurm yourself.
Need to test the Chef or Ansible code that installs your Slurm, end to end? Or debug a Slurm configuration by hand?
An unmanaged cluster brings the sind nodes, and hands Slurm over to your own tooling.
One line does it: managed false on the controller. It covers the whole cluster, so the submitter and workers are unmanaged too.
What stays the same: containers, networking, DNS and SSH access, and munge, running with a shared key.
What's missing: sind writes no Slurm configuration, and starts no Slurm daemon.
Create the cluster the usual way. Once every node runs systemd, sshd and munge, sind hands back the prompt.
Now it's your turn. By hand, sind ssh writes a slurm.conf on the controller, and all nodes share that file.
Next comes a one-line cgroup config, and then slurmctld on the controller.
Start slurmd on both workers, and the last command runs a first job across them.
Chef and Ansible reach the nodes over SSH, as root: include the SSH config sind exports, and list the node names as hosts, as in this inventory.
To debug a configuration, run slurmctld in the foreground, with full verbosity.
Backup controllers and new workers work too, and you add them to your Slurm configuration yourself.
So: managed false keeps sind out of Slurm, the nodes still come with SSH and munge, and your own tooling provisions the rest.
Next up, the guide to using CVMFS. See you there!
